title: Signed shift comparison for the augmented Roos complex
statement: For l prime, E a finite extension of Q_l, X a scheme, every cochain complex P of internal O_E,X-modules and every integer r, there is a chain isomorphism j:roos(P[r]) to roos(P)[r] such that augmentation(P[r]) followed by j is the shifted augmentation(P). This concerns the explicitly specified strict Roos complex, not an arbitrary model of a derived limit.

proof.text: Termwise tensor reduction commutes with shifts. Since the shift is an equivalence, the product comparison gives product(P[r]) isomorphic to product(P)[r]. On every product projection, the comparison commutes with one-minus-shift and identifies the product of tensor units.

In Roos degree i, use the product comparison on the first coordinate and (-1)^r times its reindexed degree i-1 component on the second. The Roos differential has entries d, one-minus-shift, zero and -d. The sign on the second coordinate makes the chain equation hold for the shifted differential. The inverse uses the inverse comparison and the same sign. The zero second coordinate of the augmentation proves the normalization equation.

lean.statement:
theorem derived_nakayama_roos_shift_comparison
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] (X : Scheme.{u})
    (P : CochainComplex (AdicCompletion.Modules l E X) ℤ) (r : ℤ) :
    ∃ j : AdicCompletion.roos l E X (P⟦r⟧) ≅ (AdicCompletion.roos l E X P)⟦r⟧,
      AdicCompletion.augmentation l E X (P⟦r⟧) ≫ j.hom =
        (AdicCompletion.augmentation l E X P)⟦r⟧'
